Meteorological Analysis (Based on 1730 hours IST)
The line of withdrawal of Southwest Monsoon  continues to pass through 27.5°N/86.5°E, Supaul, Ranchi,
Raipur, Brahmapuri, Parbhani, Baramati, Harnai and 17.5°N/71.8°E.
Conditions are likely to become favourable  for further withdrawal of southwest monsoon from most parts of
Marathwada & Vidarbha, some more parts of Maharashtra & Chhattisgarh and some parts of Telangana &
North interior Karnataka during next 2-3 days.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Sikkim & neighbourhood at 3.1 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough form northeast Bihar to Northwest Bay of Bengal across Jharkhand and Gangetic West Bengal at
0.9 km above mean sea level persists.
The trough form south Bihar to Vidarbha across East Madhya Pradesh persists and now seen between 3.1 &
5.8 km above mean sea level.
The upper air cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar & adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu at 0.9 km above
mean sea level persists.
The trough from above cyclonic circulation over Gulf of Mannar & adjoining south coastal Tamil Nadu to
Eastcentral Arabian Sea across interior Tamil Nadu and north Kerala at 0.9 km above mean sea level persists.

Agromet advisories for various parts of the country
Agromet advisories for likely impact of Heavy Rainfall
In Sub Himalayan West Bengal, drainout excess water from rice fields, black gram, green gram and
vegetables. Harvest cardamom and keep in safer places.  Provide bamboo stakes to Dalle Khorsani (chilli)
plants to prevent lodging and stem breakage.
In Keralam, ensure effective drainage from paddy, banana, coconut, pepper, ginger, turmeric, vegetables and
other standing crops, with priority to low-lying and waterlogged fields. Provide strong support to banana and
other vulnerable crops, strengthen drainage around plantations and postpone irrigation, fertilizer application and
plant-protection operations until field conditions improve.
In Tamil Nadu, drain excess water from rice, sorghum, maize, black gram and vegetable fields. Undertake
detrashing and propping of sugarcane and provide adequate support to banana, papaya and moringa to
prevent lodging. Harvest mature paddy wherever conditions permit and keep harvested grains in dry storage.
In Coastal Karnataka, maintain effective drainage in standing crop fields to prevent waterlogging and keep
drainage channels clear. Provide mechanical support to banana and papaya plantations and staking to young
plants and vegetables; undertake propping in sugarcane to minimise lodging.
In South Interior Karnataka, maintain proper drainage in standing crop fields and remove excess rainwater
promptly from low-lying areas. Postpone irrigation, intercultural operations, fertilizer and plant-protection
applications while fields remain wet, and provide staking/propping support to vulnerable crops.
In Arunachal Pradesh, maintain proper drainage in rice, finger millet, soybean and vegetable fields to remove
excess water and prevent waterlogging. Harvest mature upland/Jhum rice, finger millet, soybean and
vegetables during suitable dry intervals and move the produce to safe, covered storage.
In Assam and Meghalaya, maintain effective drainage in rice, maize, soybean, pigeon pea and vegetable
fields, keeping field channels clear to prevent waterlogging. In Assam, maintain drainage furrows in pigeon pea
and protect sugarcane from lodging; harvest mature jute and vegetables wherever conditions permit and
postpone fertilizer, pesticide and other field operations during wet conditions. 
 Agromet advisories for likely impact of Thunderstorm / Gusty Winds
Shift the harvested produce in safer places or cover the produce with tarpaulin sheets in the fields. Tie the
harvested crops securely and cover them to minimize the risk of displacement from strong surface winds.
Provide mechanical support to horticultural crops and staking or support to vegetables and young fruit plants /
fruit-bearing plants to avoid lodging due to strong winds.
 Advisories for likely impact of Heavy Rainfall for Livestock / Poultry / Fisheries 
Keep the animals inside the shed during heavy rainfall and provide them balanced feed.
Store the feed and fodder in a safe place to prevent spoilage.
Construct an outlet with proper netting around the ponds to drain excess water, thereby preventing fish from
escaping in the event of overflow.
